Code 30/6/1. 24 pages (idx 0-23): idx 0 bilingual cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions + Hindi Q1; English on every even index 2-22, Hindi on every odd index 1-21 (each the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked, all Hindi (idx 17 opens with the Hindi Q35 table and Hindi Q36, idx 19 Hindi Q37, idx 21 Hindi Q38); idx 23 is blank (QR and folio only, no English, no ghost); last English page idx 22. No usable text layer: every row read off the page images. General Instructions (i)-(x) confirm full80: 38 questions, A Q1-18 MCQ + Q19-20 A-R @1, B Q21-25 @2, C Q26-31 @3, D Q32-35 @5, E Q36-38 case studies @4. Instruction (viii) prints 2 internal choices in B, 2 in C, 2 in D and 3 in E: Q21, Q25, Q27, Q29, Q32, Q34, Q36, Q37, Q38, all found on the paper, and the marking-scheme walk shows exactly these nine OR blocks and no other. Main-question alternatives are printed (A)/(B); the case-study alternatives are printed as an unlabelled OR inside part (ii) (worth 2), so refs follow the addendum: Q36iia/Q36iib with part (iii) worth 1 (instruction (vii) says the choice sits in the 2-mark question). Q38 prints NO per-part marks on the paper; 1/2/1 is taken from the marking scheme's split. Section-A keys read off the marking scheme for 30/6/1 as images and each re-derived: all 20 agree; no void notes anywhere in the scheme. Decimal points are ORDINARY full stops on this paper (Q8 20.25 cm, Q10 2.25 cm), although the marking scheme prints raised dots (2·25, 134·8). The dots after the fractions closing Q23 and Q30 are sentence full stops, written as ordinary ones. Section E prints no 'Case Study - N' headings, so no _caseStudyLabel. The A-R block opens with the bold heading 'Assertion - Reason Based Questions :'; that heading is left out of context, the instruction sentence is kept as printed. Opener of series 30/6 (plan.txt: no reference papers): nothing skipped.

questions.context: In question numbers 19 and 20, a statement of Assertion (A) is followed by a statement of Reason (R). Choose the correct option out of the following :
questions.stem:
**Statement A (Assertion) :** If \(5 + \sqrt{7}\) is a root of a quadratic equation with rational co-efficients, then its other root is \(5 - \sqrt{7}\).

**Statement R (Reason) :** Surd roots of a quadratic equation with rational co-efficients occur in conjugate pairs.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true; and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true; but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.context:
A coaching institute of Mathematics conducts classes in two batches I and II and fees for rich and poor children are different. In batch I, there are 20 poor and 5 rich children, whereas in batch II, there are 5 poor and 25 rich children. The total monthly collection of fees from batch I is ₹ 9000 and from batch II is ₹ 26,000. Assume that each poor child pays ₹ \(x\) per month and each rich child pays ₹ \(y\) per month.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Represent the information given above in terms of \(x\) and \(y\).

questions.context:
Radio towers are used for transmitting a range of communication services including radio and television. The tower will either act as an antenna itself or support one or more antennas on its structure. On a similar concept, a radio station tower was built in two Sections A and B. Tower is supported by wires from a point O.

Distance between the base of the tower and point O is 36 cm. From point O, the angle of elevation of the top of the Section B is \(30^\circ\) and the angle of elevation of the top of Section A is \(45^\circ\).

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: Find the length of the wire from the point O to the top of Section B.

questions._figure: DECORATIVE - a photograph of pool balls and a cue on a table; every fact is in the passage. Page idx 22.
questions.context:
“Eight Ball” is a game played on a pool table with 15 balls numbered 1 to 15 and a “cue ball” that is solid and white. Of the 15 numbered balls, eight are solid (non-white) coloured and numbered 1 to 8 and seven are striped balls numbered 9 to 15.

The 15 numbered pool balls (no cue ball) are placed in a large bowl and mixed, then one ball is drawn out at random.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
questions.stem: What is the probability that the drawn ball bears number 8 ?
